feedback: If the learner thinks nothing is moving because they cannot see it: the streamer/pinwheel moves because invisible air is pushing against it.
Connect the observed flow to its cause: the air is moving toward where warm air has risen and left a gap.
activities.intendedInsight: Air itself is invisible, but its movement can be detected through its effects — and those effects are evidence of air flowing, which is what wind is.
learnerActions: Use streamers, smoke traces, or a pinwheel to detect moving air you cannot see
Observe which way the indicators point and describe the direction and strength of the air movement
Relate what the indicators show back to warm air rising somewhere and cooler air flowing in
activities.title: Make the invisible air visible

feedback: If the order is muddled: start from what the Sun does first (heats the surface unevenly) and follow what happens to the air step by step.
For the night case: the land is now the cooler surface, so the rising happens over the sea and air flows out from the land — the breeze reverses.

For the open ocean: wind still occurs because the Sun heats different parts of the Earth (sea, land, near and far) by different amounts, so air keeps moving, and that moving air can travel far across the ocean; trees and hills are not needed.
activities.intendedInsight: The learner can state and apply the full chain of causes, not just recite that wind exists, and can use it to predict wind direction in new situations.
learnerActions: Arrange the steps of the causal chain in order: uneven heating → warm air rises → cooler air moves in → wind
In your own words, explain why a breeze often blows from the sea onto the land on a hot afternoon
Predict and explain which way the breeze blows at night when the land cools faster than the sea
Decide whether there could be wind over the open ocean with no trees or hills, and say what causes it
activities.title: Order the causal chain and explain the sea breeze

feedback: If the retelling drops a step, point to the missing link (what makes the air rise, or what fills the gap).
If the learner says equal heating would still make wind: with no uneven heating there is no reason for air to rise and be replaced, so there would be little or no wind from this cause.
activities.intendedInsight: The same causal chain can be put into words and reasoned about in dialogue, reinforcing the explanation the learner has observed.
learnerActions: Pose the question 'why does the wind blow?' and listen to or read an explanation that narrates uneven heating, rising warm air, and cooler air moving in
Retell the chain back and ask a follow-up, such as what would happen if the Sun heated everywhere equally
activities.title: Ask a weather expert why the wind blows
